reviews.reason: Libsecret and pkg-config installation is present before desktop build and non-server tests. Keep GitHub-hosted runners, fork ledger checks and fork branch triggers instead of upstream Blacksmith infrastructure. Server test shards remain separate. Fork-only authoring guards block against the selected head's upstream base; a pushed historical rewrite can suppress replayed authoring warnings only after proving its full tree equals the live fork source. Every other branch is offered the rebase-rehearsal scope, which suppresses them only after the scan proves the head omits the trunk and sits on a tagged upstream commit the trunk has not reached. The separately named live-upstream scan stays advisory so unrelated upstream drift does not fail a PR. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260905.1290: the fork adopts upstream's repo-wide knip:check step, and declines the setup-apt-mirrors action and the Blacksmith mirror rewrite because every fork job runs on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners where those mirror files do not exist. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260906.1303 with no fork change: relative to that review upstream only adds the `Test nightly release checks` step running `node --test .github/scripts/check-nightly-release.test.cjs`, an upstream-only self-test for release scripts the fork never ships; the fork keeps no equivalent step because its nightly/release flow lives in `hyprws-release.yml`. Reviewed again at v0.0.41-nightly.20260908.1414 with no fork change: relative to that review upstream only widens its Rust job, renaming `Check resource monitor formatting` and `Test resource monitor` into `Check Rust formatting` and `Test Rust crates` loops over `resource-monitor`, `kde-snap-shot` and `hyprland-snap-shot`; the fork CI runs no Rust job at all, so there is no fork step for that widening to land on.

Libsecret and pkg-config are installed before preflight tests and Linux artifact build; ImageMagick remains installed in the build job. Keep Linux x64 AppImage-only fork releases, fork stable/nightly versioning and pruning; upstream multi-platform signing and publication do not apply. The release checkout is now recorded before dependency setup, expected assets come from the actual build, and an always-run fork outcome job verifies tag/asset publication and retains failures for release-only retry. Runner-temporary export paths stay in step scope where the runner context is valid, with one shared filename for retention and upload; the required semantic guard keeps an unconditional nonempty receipt check between collection and upload, while missing upload inputs remain a hard error. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260905.1290 with no fork change: the setup-apt-mirrors steps target Blacksmith runners the fork does not use, and the Visual Studio Spectre component rename only affects the Windows build the Linux-only fork release never runs. Reviewed again at v0.0.39-nightly.20260906.1303 with no fork change: relative to that review upstream reverts `check_changes` to the `actions/github-script` release-gap check with the `8,38 * * * *` schedule, while the fork keeps its newer tag-compare shape (`Compare hyprws to last nightly tag`, `needs: preflight`) which already supersedes both upstream variants; the comment-only `check_changes` skip note does not apply to the fork job graph. Reviewed again at v0.0.41-nightly.20260908.1414 with no fork change: upstream replaces `check_changes` with a `resolve_commit` job so a manual stable dispatch builds the commit of the latest published nightly, which does not apply because the fork cuts stable from a snapshot branch the sync walk records rather than from a dispatch input; and upstream adds a `Cache Linux capture helpers` step plus `T3CODE_DESKTOP_REUSE_LINUX_CAPTURE_HELPERS` for the two new snap-shot crates, which the fork declines because its Linux job installs the Rust toolchain unconditionally and caches no crate, so both helpers are built from source on every release. Upstream's new `deploy_marketing` job is nightly marketing publication the fork does not run. Fork change for RSI-Software/t3code-hyprws#738 with no upstream counterpart: the Linux build job now packs the server into an `npm pack`-shaped tarball after the desktop artifact and publishes it beside the AppImage, because the fork ships no npm package and the pinned-runtime installer resolves a fork version to that release asset instead of a registry spec (apps/server/src/cloud/forkRuntimeRelease.ts). The pack step first asserts the built server reports the release version: the launcher names each pinned directory after the version it asked for while the client reports the version baked into its bundle, so a differently stamped bundle would make every boot retry the same update forever. Upstream needs none of this because its releases publish to npm. Reviewed again for the fork-only outcome job: its checkout now carries `token: ${{ secrets.HYPRWS_MIRROR_TOKEN }}` with default credential persistence instead of `persist-credentials: false` plus a hand-built `http.extraheader` in the receipt step. Upstream has no outcome job, so there is no upstream counterpart for this change. `persist-credentials: false` made the action run its auth removal in the main step, where `git submodule foreach --recursive` exits 128 on gitlinks `.gitmodules` does not declare, so the job never wrote a receipt; the required nonempty receipt check between collection and upload is unchanged.
